<?xml version="1.0"?>
<rdf:RDF xmlns="http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich/"
     xml:base="http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich/"
     xmlns:owl="http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#"
     xmlns:rdf="http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#"
     xmlns:xml="http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace"
     xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#"
     xmlns:rdfs="http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#">
    <owl:Ontology rdf:about="http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich">
        <rdfs:comment xml:lang="en">This is an ontology describing a Sandwich</rdfs:comment>
    </owl:Ontology>
    


    <!-- 
    ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
    //
    // Object Properties
    //
    ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
     -->

    


    <!-- http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#hasBaseBread -->

    <owl:ObjectProperty rdf:about="http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#hasBaseBread">
        <rdfs:domain rdf:resource="http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#Deck"/>
        <rdfs:range rdf:resource="http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#Bread"/>
    </owl:ObjectProperty>
    


    <!-- http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#hasClosingBread -->

    <owl:ObjectProperty rdf:about="http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#hasClosingBread">
        <rdfs:domain rdf:resource="http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#Sandwich"/>
        <rdfs:range rdf:resource="http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#ClosingBread"/>
    </owl:ObjectProperty>
    


    <!-- http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#hasDeck -->

    <owl:ObjectProperty rdf:about="http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#hasDeck">
        <rdfs:domain rdf:resource="http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#Sandwich"/>
        <rdfs:range rdf:resource="http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#Deck"/>
    </owl:ObjectProperty>
    


    <!-- http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#hasFilling -->

    <owl:ObjectProperty rdf:about="http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#hasFilling">
        <rdfs:domain rdf:resource="http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#Deck"/>
        <rdfs:range rdf:resource="http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#Filling"/>
    </owl:ObjectProperty>
    


    <!-- http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#isOnTopOf -->

    <owl:ObjectProperty rdf:about="http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#isOnTopOf">
        <rdf:type rdf:resource="http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#AsymmetricProperty"/>
        <rdf:type rdf:resource="http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#IrreflexiveProperty"/>
        <rdfs:domain rdf:resource="http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#Deck"/>
        <rdfs:range rdf:resource="http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#Deck"/>
    </owl:ObjectProperty>
    


    <!-- 
    ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
    //
    // Classes
    //
    ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
     -->

    


    <!-- http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#Bread -->

    <owl:Class rdf:about="http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#Bread"/>
    


    <!-- http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#Cheese -->

    <owl:Class rdf:about="http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#Cheese">
        <rdfs:subClassOf rdf:resource="http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#Filling"/>
    </owl:Class>
    


    <!-- http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#ClosingBread -->

    <owl:Class rdf:about="http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#ClosingBread">
        <rdfs:subClassOf rdf:resource="http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#Bread"/>
    </owl:Class>
    


    <!-- http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#Deck -->

    <owl:Class rdf:about="http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#Deck">
        <rdfs:subClassOf>
            <owl:Restriction>
                <owl:onProperty rdf:resource="http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#hasFilling"/>
                <owl:someValuesFrom rdf:resource="http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#Filling"/>
            </owl:Restriction>
        </rdfs:subClassOf>
        <rdfs:subClassOf>
            <owl:Restriction>
                <owl:onProperty rdf:resource="http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#hasBaseBread"/>
                <owl:qualifiedCardinality rdf:datatype="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#nonNegativeInteger">1</owl:qualifiedCardinality>
                <owl:onClass rdf:resource="http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#Bread"/>
            </owl:Restriction>
        </rdfs:subClassOf>
        <rdfs:subClassOf>
            <owl:Restriction>
                <owl:onProperty rdf:resource="http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#isOnTopOf"/>
                <owl:maxQualifiedCardinality rdf:datatype="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#nonNegativeInteger">1</owl:maxQualifiedCardinality>
                <owl:onClass rdf:resource="http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#Deck"/>
            </owl:Restriction>
        </rdfs:subClassOf>
    </owl:Class>
    


    <!-- http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#Filling -->

    <owl:Class rdf:about="http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#Filling"/>
    


    <!-- http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#Meat -->

    <owl:Class rdf:about="http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#Meat">
        <rdfs:subClassOf rdf:resource="http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#Filling"/>
    </owl:Class>
    


    <!-- http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#OtherProtein -->

    <owl:Class rdf:about="http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#OtherProtein">
        <rdfs:subClassOf rdf:resource="http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#Filling"/>
    </owl:Class>
    


    <!-- http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#Sandwich -->

    <owl:Class rdf:about="http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#Sandwich">
        <rdfs:subClassOf>
            <owl:Restriction>
                <owl:onProperty rdf:resource="http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#hasDeck"/>
                <owl:minQualifiedCardinality rdf:datatype="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#nonNegativeInteger">1</owl:minQualifiedCardinality>
                <owl:onClass rdf:resource="http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#Deck"/>
            </owl:Restriction>
        </rdfs:subClassOf>
        <rdfs:subClassOf>
            <owl:Restriction>
                <owl:onProperty rdf:resource="http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#hasClosingBread"/>
                <owl:maxQualifiedCardinality rdf:datatype="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#nonNegativeInteger">1</owl:maxQualifiedCardinality>
                <owl:onClass rdf:resource="http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#ClosingBread"/>
            </owl:Restriction>
        </rdfs:subClassOf>
    </owl:Class>
    


    <!-- http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#Spread -->

    <owl:Class rdf:about="http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#Spread">
        <rdfs:subClassOf rdf:resource="http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#Filling"/>
    </owl:Class>
    


    <!-- http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#Vegetable -->

    <owl:Class rdf:about="http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#Vegetable">
        <rdfs:subClassOf rdf:resource="http://www.leeds.ac.uk/xckx3323/ontologies/sandwich#Filling"/>
    </owl:Class>
</rdf:RDF>

Report on Sandwich Ontology Design 
 
The designed ontology attempts to model the components and structure of a sandwich as 
described by the Wikipedia article, as per the project guidelines. 
At first the article describes a sandwich to be a piece of food consisting of one or more 
fillings between two pieces of bread. It mentions a wide variety of possible fillings, as well as 
the possibility for there to be a number of pieces of bread different than two, introducing the 
concepts of a “sandwich deck”, and that of an “open sandwich”. Multi-deck sandwiches may 
introduce multiple additional layers of bread and filling, while open sandwiches omit the need 
for a top bread. These special cases make the initial proposition for the definition of a 
sandwich being “bread-filling-bread” obsolete, as the number of pieces of bread is no longer 
fixed. 
To accommodate all special cases, the ontology was designed to think of sandwiches in a 
different way. The core of an open sandwich – our base case – is a base of bread, and some 
fillings. This open sandwich can then become closed with a further addition of a top bread, or 
be complemented by a second deck. An interesting observation can be made that even 
sandwiches with the original 2 slices of bread can have some of their fillings on top, as are 
the cases with the Croque monsieur and the Portuguese Francesinha. The ontology views 
those cases as “open two-deck sandwiches”, threating the de-facto closing bread with 
additional toppings simply as a second deck. 
 
The ontology includes the following ten classes: 
• Sandwich: the root class. 
• Deck: composing of Bread and Filling. 
• Bread, with subclass ClosingBread. 
• Filling, with five subclasses: Meat, Cheese, Veg, Spread, and OtherProtein. 
 
The “ClosingBread” subclass was chosen for specificity in object properties we will later see, 
but also because many times the top bread of a sandwich has particularities, as is the case 
with hamburgers for example. 
The Filling classes chosen were all top-level fillings, with the intent of covering as much 
ground as possible. “Spread” can be applied to both sweet and savory spreads. 
“OtherProtein” is an attempt to fit in miscellaneous items in sandwiches serving that 
particular purpose, such as eggs, tofu, or hashbrowns. No hierarchy was applied there, 
because of the constraint of there being up to five object properties. 
 
All five object properties were needed to describe a sandwich, given the above classes: 
1. hasDeck (Sandwich → Deck): must have at least one deck to be a sandwich. 
2. hasBaseBread (Deck → Bread): each Deck must have a base slice. 
3. hasFilling (Deck → Filling): a deck must contain one or more fillings.

[PAGE 2]
4. hasClosingBread (Sandwich → ClosingBread): optional top bread. 
5. isOnTopOf (Deck → Deck): to model the vertical order of decks in a sandwich. 
 
This provides a comprehensive list of the possible relationship between all classes, as they 
were defined. Sandwiches are comprised of at least one deck and an optional closing bread. 
Any deck has a base and a filling. The order of decks is modelled with the “isOnTopOf” 
relationship. 
 
To complete the ontology, the above structural restrictions are formalized as a set of axioms: 
 
1. Any sandwich must contain at least one deck: 
- Sandwich ⊑ (≥1 hasDeck.Deck) 
 
2. A sandwich may contain at most one closing bread: 
- Sandwich ⊑ (≤1 hasClosingBread.ClosingBread) 
 
3. Every deck needs to have exactly one base bread: 
- Deck ⊑ (=1 hasBaseBread.Bread) 
 
4. Every deck must contain one or more fillings: 
- Deck ⊑ (≥1 hasFilling.Filling) 
 
5. Two decks cannot be on top of one another at the same time: 
- Asymmetric(isOnTopOf) 
 
6. No deck can be on top of itself: 
- Irreflexive(isOnTopOf) 
 
With this, the ontology provides a comprehensive structure for describing most sandwiches, 
within the required number of classes and properties. The design allows for the inference of 
wether a sandwich is open or closed, as well as knowledge of how the decks are stacked, 
without allowing for an obvious paradox to occur. The modular design of the ontology allows 
for the addition of further classes, such as a open and closed sandwiches, and the addition 
of hierarchy within the Filling top class. 
With the constraint on the number of properties allowed, however, some obvious limitations 
arised. The “Filling” set of  subclasses don’t have a relationship to encode the order they 
appear in, as is possible with decks. Additionally, there are no clear restrictions on two 
individuals using the same component instance, like sharing a closing bread for example.
